---
title: "codeminer"
---

Python client for the [CodeMiner](https://github.com/codeminer-io/codeminer) clinical code API.

## Installation

```bash
uv add codeminer
```

Or with pip:

```bash
pip install codeminer
```

For the latest development version, install from GitHub:

```bash
pip install git+https://github.com/codeminer-io/codeminer-py
```

## Connecting to the API

Point the client at your CodeMiner API server:

```python
import codeminer

# Set the API URL (defaults to http://127.0.0.1:8000)
codeminer.config.base_url = "http://your-server:8000"

# Verify the connection
codeminer.check_api_connection()
```

Alternatively, set the `CODEMINER_BASE_URL` environment variable.

## Quick Start

```python
from codeminer import (
    DESCRIPTION, CODES, CODES_LIKE, CHILDREN, N_CHILDREN,
    PARENTS, MAP, check_api_connection, AND, OR, NOT, with_type
)
```

### Searching for codes

```python
# Search by description
asthma = DESCRIPTION("asthma", type="ICD-10")

# Search by code pattern
j45_codes = CODES_LIKE("^J45", type="ICD-10")

# Look up specific codes
codes = CODES("J45", "E11", type="ICD-10")
```

### Navigating hierarchies

```python
# The code and all of its descendants
descendants = CHILDREN("73211009", type="SNOMED CT")

# The code and its descendants, one level down
children = N_CHILDREN("73211009", depth=1, type="SNOMED CT")

# The code and all of its ancestors
parents = PARENTS("73211009", type="SNOMED CT")
```

### Mapping between code systems

```python
mapped = MAP("4939", from_type="ICD-9", to_type="ICD-10")
```

### Composing queries with infix operators

Use `>>AND>>`, `>>OR>>`, and `>>NOT>>` to combine results:

```python
diabetes = DESCRIPTION("diabet", type="ICD-10") >>AND>> (
    CHILDREN("E10", type="ICD-10") >>OR>> CHILDREN("E11", type="ICD-10")
)
```

## Configuration

### Setting persistent defaults

Use `codeminer.config` to set defaults that apply to all subsequent calls,
mirroring R's `options()` system:

```python
import codeminer

# Set default code type — no need to pass type= on every call
codeminer.config.type = "SNOMED CT"

DESCRIPTION("diabetes")          # uses SNOMED CT
CODES("73211009")                # uses SNOMED CT
CHILDREN("73211009")             # uses SNOMED CT

# MAP has its own defaults; config.type doesn't apply to it
codeminer.config.map_from = "ICD-9"
codeminer.config.map_to = "ICD-10"
MAP("4939")                      # maps ICD-9 to ICD-10

# A data frame's code type must match map_from, so clear it when passing results
codeminer.config.map_from = None
```

Available config options:

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `config.type` | `None` | Default code type (not used by MAP) |
| `config.lookup_version` | `"latest"` | Lookup table version |
| `config.relationship_version` | `"latest"` | Relationship table version |
| `config.map_version` | `"latest"` | Mapping table version |
| `config.map_from` | `None` | Default `from_type` for MAP |
| `config.map_to` | `None` | Default `to_type` for MAP |
| `config.base_url` | `None` | API URL (falls back to env var, then `http://127.0.0.1:8000`) |

Explicit function arguments always take priority over config values.

### Temporary overrides with `with_type()`

Use `with_type()` when a script is predominantly one code type but needs
to query another temporarily — mirroring R's `with_type()`. It sets both
`config.type` and `config.map_to` for the duration of the block:

```python
import codeminer
from codeminer import CODES, MAP, with_type

# Script works with SNOMED CT
codeminer.config.type = "SNOMED CT"
codeminer.config.map_to = "SNOMED CT"

# Temporarily switch to BNF for a few queries
with with_type("BNF"):
    bnf_codes = CODES("0204")

# Back to SNOMED CT
# from_type inferred from the DataFrame, to_type from config
mapped = MAP(bnf_codes)
```

Nesting is supported:

```python
codeminer.config.type = "SNOMED CT"

with with_type("ICD-10"):
    icd_codes = DESCRIPTION("diabetes")
    with with_type("BNF"):
        bnf_codes = CODES("0601")
    # back to ICD-10
    more_icd = CODES("E10")

# back to SNOMED CT
sct_codes = DESCRIPTION("diabetes")
```

### Passing previous results

Functions accept DataFrames from previous queries. The code type is
inferred from the DataFrame's `code_type` column:

```python
codeminer.config.type = "SNOMED CT"

# Build up a codelist
asthma = DESCRIPTION("asthma")
asthma_children = CHILDREN(asthma)

# Map to ICD-10 (from_type inferred, to_type set explicitly)
mapped = MAP(asthma, to_type="ICD-10")
```

### Resetting config

```python
codeminer.config.reset()  # restores all defaults
```

### Base URL resolution

The API base URL is resolved in this order:

1. Explicit `base_url` parameter on each function call
2. `codeminer.config.base_url`
3. `CODEMINER_BASE_URL` environment variable
4. Default: `http://127.0.0.1:8000`

```python
# Option 1: config
codeminer.config.base_url = "http://myserver:9000"

# Option 2: environment variable
import os
os.environ["CODEMINER_BASE_URL"] = "http://myserver:9000"

# Option 3: per-call
DESCRIPTION("asthma", type="ICD-10", base_url="http://myserver:9000")
```
